ops.title: Restart the lane supervisor service dev.long-running.lane.durable-agents (launchctl kickstart -k) once the fix installs?
ops.body:
Restart it (Recommended)
Options: Restart it (Recommended) | Restart it now | Don't restart
Notes: His own pick, verbatim option label, in the team-lead session's AskUserQuestion at about 20:03 PT on 2026-11-16. The full question as asked: "The lane supervisor has been stuck since 7:54. A GitHub-event loop lane-core added can't finish while dev keeps getting pushes, so nothing merges, wakes or posts cards. The fix is pushed, but the stuck process only picks up new code after it finishes a pass, so it needs a restart. The restart is `launchctl kickstart -k` of the lane supervisor service (dev.long-running.lane.durable-agents). That restarts the supervisor process only, not any Claude session: lane workers run as their own background jobs. Restart it once the fix installs?" The option he picked read: "Restart the lane supervisor service once the release with the fix installs, then check that passes resume and lane workers are untouched." Scope: one kickstart of that service onto the install carrying f7af1e3c7 and 95969f242 (1.0.1719 or later). The 20:18 kickstart landed on broken 1.0.1718, so the fix never installed.
